phones_sentence: County veterans service office phones and addresses come from the County Veterans Service Officers Association of Wisconsin. The association’s list prints no office hours; call before you go.

notes: Say your county and the name of the nursing home or assisted living community. In Milwaukee County, also give the ZIP code.

The state ombudsman program serves residents age 60 and older. For residents ages 18–59, the state’s health department points to a separate ombudsman program at Disability Rights Wisconsin, 800-928-8778.
Calls are answered Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m., except state holidays.

programs.name: Wisconsin veterans: accredited claims help
programs.organization: Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs and County Veterans Service Offices
programs.description: Free help from your County Veterans Service Officer and the Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs Claims Assistance Office with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits, plus state benefits.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its Veterans Service Office, or call the Wisconsin Veterans Benefits and Resource Center at 1-800-WIS-VETS (800-947-8387). For a state claims officer, call the Claims Assistance Office at 833-494-7256.
constraints: The association’s office list prints no hours; call first.
Wisconsin has Tribal Veterans Service Officers for 11 tribal nations, listed by the state department; they are not shown on county cards.

programs.name: Aging and Disability Resource Centers (statewide)
programs.description: A physical center in every county where older adults, adults with disabilities and caregivers can get information, assistance and support. Most Tribal nations have a Tribal aging and disability resource specialist. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 844-WIS-ADRC (844-947-2372) to be connected to your local center, or choose a county above for its direct number.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Wisconsin
programs.organization: Wisconsin Board on Aging and Long Term Care, Medigap Helpline
programs.description: Free, unbiased counseling on Medicare, Medigap, Medicare Advantage, employer coverage and long-term care insurance. The Medigap Helpline is Wisconsin’s statewide State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) helpline; a separate Part D and prescription drug helpline answers questions for residents age 60 and over.
programs.next_step: Call the Medigap Helpline at 800-242-1060. For Medicare Part D and prescription drug questions, call 855-677-2783.
constraints: The helpline is a telephone service; for hands-on help with enrollment and appeals, ask your ADRC for a local benefit specialist.

programs.name: Wisconsin Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
programs.organization: Wisconsin Board on Aging and Long Term Care
programs.description: Statewide advocacy for residents age 60 and older of nursing homes and assisted living, delivered by regional ombudsmen assigned by county. Volunteer ombudsmen visit facilities in some counties.
programs.next_step: Call 800-815-0015 and give the county and facility name. To report suspected abuse of an elder age 60 or over, call the Wisconsin Elder Abuse Hotline at 833-586-0107 or your county elder-adult-at-risk agency. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.
For residents ages 18–59, a separate ombudsman program is run by Disability Rights Wisconsin, 800-928-8778.

programs.name: Free legal help in Wisconsin
programs.organization: Legal Action of Wisconsin; Judicare Legal Aid
programs.description: Free civil legal help for people with low income. Legal Action of Wisconsin serves the southern 39 counties and has staff who work with veterans; Judicare Legal Aid serves the 33 northern counties. Neither handles criminal defense.
programs.next_step: In the southern counties, call Legal Action of Wisconsin’s intake line at 855-947-2529 and say you are a veteran. In the 33 northern counties, call Judicare Legal Aid at 800-472-1638.
constraints: Applicants are screened; income, case type and capacity limits apply.
Which agency serves your county depends on where you live; if the first agency cannot help, ask it for the other.

programs.name: VA medical centers serving Wisconsin
programs.description: Wisconsin is mostly in VA’s Great Lakes network (VISN 12): Clement J. Zablocki VA Medical Center in Milwaukee (414-384-2000), Tomah VA Medical Center (608-372-3971), William S. Middleton Memorial Veterans Hospital in Madison (608-256-1901) and the Oscar G. Johnson VA Medical Center in Iron Mountain, Michigan. The northwest corner is in VISN 23, served from VA Minneapolis. Community clinics are listed in VA’s facility locator.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: The state’s page names regions rather than counties, so this card does not assign counties. Your VA care team may be at a different clinic or system; follow what VA tells you.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 72 counties have a county veterans service office, an Aging and Disability Resource Center and a long-term care ombudsman line. Ombudsmen are assigned by county, but the state publishes one statewide line, so every county shows it.
coverage_note: County veterans service office addresses and phones come from the County Veterans Service Officers Association of Wisconsin list, which prints no hours. Aging and Disability Resource Centers come from the state health department’s listing, read as search excerpts of a paginated page. The long-term care ombudsman line comes from the Board on Aging and Long Term Care. Independent Living Centers come from the state health department’s center list. Reviewed November 15, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
